content.title: USA 2, Belgium 5: Pochettino’s Americans flop in pre-World Cup test
content.text: ATLANTA – The U.S. men’s national team hoped that these spring friendlies, the last before coach Mauricio Pochettino selects his World Cup roster, would reinforce the positive momentum of the fall.Instead, a deflating loss served as a warning for what can come against some of the world’s best teams and against the game’s attacking players.Saturday’s game against Belgium, a top-10 European opponent, was the type of test that could show how ready this American team is for a home World Cup. Pochettino’s lineup featured most of the country’s biggest stars: Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie, Folarin Balogun, Antonee Robinson and Tim Weah. But despite a bright start, Belgium found its stride just before halftime and in the first 15 minutes of the second half, with Manchester City winger Jérémy Doku setting the pace as the Red Devils eased to a 5-2 win.The U.S. played some of its best soccer under Pochettino through the first 45 minutes. It looked confident and aggressive, matched up well athletically with Belgium and created numerous dangerous opportunities. And it was the Americans who broke through first when Weston McKennie beat Nicolas Raskin to Robinson’s corner kick to direct it home with his right foot in the 39th minute.But as much as the U.S. looked the better side for stretches in the first half, Belgium still was dangerous nearly every time it advanced into the U.S.’s defensive third.Doku, especially, made life miserable for the Americans. He created a superb chance in the 37th minute, and then in the 45th minute, Belgium found an equalizer when Doku’s dangerous run down the left forced a Matt Turner save. The ball bounced outside the 18-yard-box and into the path of Zeno Debast, who stung a lovely finish inside the far post.It was Doku again that created repeated chances in the second half. His danger down the left set up Amadou Onana’s easy finish from the top of the box in the 53rd minute, and it was the Man City man’s attack that forced a fantastic save from Turner, but only after a handball caught by VAR that resulted in Belgium’s penalty in the 59th minute. Charles De Ketelaere finished the spot kick to secure the victory.Dodi Lukebakio added a fourth in the 68th minute, and some fans turned and headed toward the exits. All they missed was Lukebakio’s second in the 82nd, and a Patrick Agyemang goal off the bench that accounted for the final margin.Here’s a closer look at the match:Belgium players had plenty to celebrate in a rout of the USA.Dirk Waem / Belga Mag / AFP / Getty ImagesHow things fell off the railsThe game fell apart in a 15-minute stretch in the second half.After getting to the 45th minute with a 1-0 lead, the U.S. allowed goals in the 45th minute, and then in the 53rd and 59th on the other side of the halftime break.The U.S. just seemed to struggle with some of the individual brilliance of Belgium, namely Doku, down its right wing. The Manchester City man was giving fits to Weah, a natural winger playing right back, and McKenzie, the center back trying to win a job on the World Cup roster. Little things led to big chances — allowing players to turn in the box, failing to clear the ball or allow cutbacks. The U.S. went from being right in the game to being a step behind Belgium at nearly every turn. After those three deflating goals and mass substitutions, the quality gap started to grow bigger and Belgium kept cruising. The goals from Lukebakio made a bad day even worse. Neither felt like the U.S. put up much of a fight.The Americans won’t have much time to regroup before facing another top team in Portugal on Tuesday.Turner gets his chance, but is there a GK competition?Matt Freese started 12 consecutive games for the USMNT to close 2025. When he got both games in October, and then when Turner was left off the roster entirely in November, it seemed that the job was firmly Freese’s.So, when Turner got the starting nod Saturday, for the first time since a 4-0 loss to Switzerland last June, heads turned. But Turner didn’t exactly grasp the job with both hands — and followed up those four goals against in his last U.S. outing with five this time.From a shot-stopping perspective, he wasn’t terrible. He made a few decent saves. He perhaps could have done better on Belgium’s first-half goal, but perhaps not. All four open-play goals were well taken, and the other was a penalty.His most alarming mistake of all actually came in the buildup to a disallowed Belgium goal. Turner, under relatively little pressure with the ball at his feet, tried to play a lofted pass to a wide-open McKennie… and over-hit it by 10 yards. Belgium immediately came the other way. Doku beat Weah to the endline, fizzed in a cross, and Turner palmed it into the body of a Belgian attacker, who scored — but with his hand.It’s unclear what to make of Turner getting the start. Is he in contention to be the No. 1 at the World Cup? Or is this Pochettino making sure that he has two goalkeepers ready to play in June, if something were to happen to Freese?We’ll get another hint, though not a definitive answer, on Tuesday against Portugal.Either way, though, given how Saturday went, it still seems like Freese’s job to lose.Matt Turner got a chance in goal for the U.S. vs. Belgium.Jared C. Tilton / Getty ImagesWho hurt/helped their World Cup causeIn these final two friendlies ahead of the World Cup cutdown, all eyes were going to be on which players made a strong case for inclusion.Johnny Cardoso’s start in midfield was a big one. The Atlético Madrid man had not been able to translate club form to the international stage. The Brazilian-American put in an OK shift against Belgium. He didn’t have any major mistakes, but also didn’t necessarily distinguish himself in the 45 minutes he played. Pochettino opted to sub him out at halftime, perhaps because he’ll get another start on Tuesday against Portugal and another chance to make his case. If not, that’ll be telling.Mark McKenzie and Turner also had big opportunities to win starting jobs. McKenzie, starting due to injuries to Chris Richards and Miles Robinson, was solid for most of his outing, but he allowed Doku to cut back too easily on the first goal of the second half.Turner will feel miserable that he let four goals by him in his first game since last summer. The U.S. lost that game, 4-0, in what felt like a wake-up call before the Gold Cup. Turner wasn’t egregious on Belgium’s goals, but anytime you see four go by you, it’s a bad day.It gets a bit harder to judge other players after the mass substitutions in the second half. Roldan entered for Cardoso at halftime and was on the field when the U.S. gave up three goals, but the fault won’t fall on the Seattle midfielder.Sebastian Berhalter’s mistake with a mishandled clearance in the 82nd minute led directly to a Lukebakio goal, which won’t help the Vancouver midfielder’s cause in a crowded midfield battle.Ricardo Pepi’s press and Patrick Agyemang’s goal will be bright spots for the forwards who are trying to secure their place this summer, even if it came down four goals late in the game.Kit clash, hydration breaks complicate friendlyBefore Saturday’s friendly even kicked off, when the players stripped off their anthem jackets, fans looked on with confusion. They saw two kits that clearly clashed, and made the match hard to decipher.Then, in the 23rd minute, many fans moaned. Some booed. The referee had whistled for a hydration break — even though the match, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, was being played indoors.The mandatory hydration breaks are a FIFA invention for the 2026 World Cup, and they were implemented here to replicate World Cup conditions. But they killed the game’s momentum. Nondescript music played. Some fans left their seats and filed up to the concourse, presumably for either a bathroom trip or food and drink.The same protocol will presumably be in place for Tuesday’s match against Portugal, which kicks off a little after 7 p.m. ET at the same Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.Pulisic still lacking in the final thirdChristian Pulisic has not scored in 2026, and has not scored for the USMNT since 2024. His drought continued Saturday, and — as has been the case at times at AC Milan over the past few months — he didn’t look sharp.He worked hard. This was one of his better defensive games for the national team.But on the ball, he was nowhere near his best. He had one threatening run early, but his finish was somewhat weak. He then lost the ball multiple times in the USMNT’s own defensive half, and didn’t offer much the rest of the first half.Early in the second, having moved from the left to a more central position, Pulisic grew into the game. He wriggled into the box, but blazed a left-footed shot high and wide. He ran at the heart of the Belgian defense twice, but couldn’t quite unlock it.Pulisic’s form is not a grave concern. He still has plenty of time to get right between now and June 12. But it’s definitely a concern. He’ll very likely need to be a catalyst if the USMNT is going to make a run this summer. And he simply hasn’t been that very often under Pochettino.
